title: Robin's inequality and the Riemann hypothesis
abstract: Let $f(n)=\sigma(n)/e^\gamma n\log\log n$, $n=3,4,\ldots$ , where $\sigma$ denotes the sum of divisors function. In 1984 Robin proved that the inequality $f(n)>1$, for all $n\ge 5041$, is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis. Here we show that the values of $f$ are close to $0$ on a set of asymptotic density $1$. Similarly, an inequality by Rosser and Schoenfeld of 1962, dealing with the Euler totient function $\varphi$, is essential only on "thin" subsets of $\mathbf{N}$.
venue: Proceedings of the Japan Academy Series A Mathematical Sciences
